name: Stepper
description: A visual progress indicator for sequential processes. Works in two modes: navigation (interactive multi-step wizard where the consumer controls Next/Back) and display (read-only status tracker like a delivery timeline). Supports horizontal and vertical orientations, numbered or dots indicator styles, explicit completion tracking, per-step error state, and configurable click navigation.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently active step value (controlled mode). Marks which StepperItem is highlighted as active.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial active step value (uncontrolled mode). Internal state is managed by the component.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback fired when a step is clicked and navigation occurs. Omit for pure display mode.

props.name: completedSteps
props.description: Array of step values explicitly marked as completed. Steps in this array show a check icon and have their connector lines lit. Consumer owns this state — it is not auto-computed.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction. Horizontal renders steps left-to-right; vertical stacks them top-to-bottom with a side connector line.

props.name: variant
props.description: Indicator style. "numbered" shows the step index; completed steps replace the number with a check icon. "dots" shows a filled circle with no number; completed steps show a check icon.

props.name: clickable
props.description: Controls which steps respond to click for navigation. "none" — no steps are clickable (ideal for display mode). "completed" — only completed steps can be clicked (go back). "all" — all non-disabled steps can be clicked (free navigation).

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes merged via cn() on the root div.

accessibility.role: StepperList renders as an <ol> (ordered list). Each StepperItem renders as an <li>. The active step's <li> receives aria-current="step".
accessibility.keyboard: When clickable is "completed" or "all", step indicators render as <button> elements and are reachable via Tab. When clickable is "none", indicators render as <div> and are not in the tab order.
accessibility.aria: aria-current="step" is set on the active StepperItem. Each clickable indicator has an aria-label of "Paso N: title".
accessibility.notes: Color alone does not convey step state — icons (check, X) and aria-current are also used. Ensure step titles are descriptive enough to be meaningful without visual context.

recommendations.description: Use completedSteps to explicitly track which steps are done. Update it as the user advances through the wizard.
Use display mode (no onValueChange, clickable="none") for read-only status indicators like delivery trackers.
recommendations.code:
<Stepper value="transito" completedSteps={["recibido", "preparacion"]}>
  <StepperList>
    <StepperItem value="recibido" title="Pedido recibido" description="24 feb, 10:32" />
    <StepperItem value="transito" title="En camino" description={<Badge variant="gray">En ruta</Badge>} />
    <StepperItem value="entregado" title="Entregado" />
  </StepperList>
</Stepper>

recommendations.description: Do not rely on the step order to auto-compute completedSteps — the component never infers completion. Always pass completedSteps explicitly.
recommendations.code:
// Wrong — steps before value are NOT auto-completed
<Stepper value="step3">
  ...
</Stepper>

recommendations.description: Do not use Stepper as a tab bar or for non-sequential navigation. It is designed for ordered, progressive flows.
recommendations.code:
// Wrong — use Tabs for non-sequential switching
<Stepper value={activeTab} clickable="all">
  ...
</Stepper>

blocks.content:
<Stepper value="..." completedSteps={[...]}>
  <StepperList>
    <StepperItem value="..." title="..." description="..." />
    <StepperItem value="..." title="..." error />
    <StepperItem value="..." title="..." disabled />
  </StepperList>
</Stepper>

rows: Unique identifier for this step. Used as the lookup key in Stepper's value and completedSteps props.
Step label rendered below (horizontal) or beside (vertical) the indicator.
Optional secondary content below the title. Accepts ReactNode for rich content like timestamps or badges.
When true, renders the step in an error state: destructive-colored indicator with an X icon. Takes priority over all other states.
When true, prevents this step from being clicked even when the Stepper's clickable prop allows navigation.
Additional CSS classes merged via cn() on the <li> element.

blocks.content: The consumer owns navigation state. The Stepper renders only the step indicators — content panels, Next/Back buttons, and validation logic all live outside the component.
Omit onValueChange and leave clickable at its default "none" to create a purely informational status display. The description prop accepts ReactNode for rich content like dates or badges.

<Stepper value="transito" completedSteps={["recibido", "preparacion"]}>
  <StepperList>
    <StepperItem value="recibido" title="Pedido recibido" description="24 feb, 10:32" />
    <StepperItem value="preparacion" title="En preparación" description="24 feb, 11:15" />
    <StepperItem
      value="transito"
      title="En camino"
      description={<Badge variant="gray">En ruta</Badge>}
    />
    <StepperItem value="entregado" title="Entregado" description="Est. 25 feb" />
  </StepperList>
</Stepper>
